photos.question: The nurse is mixing regular insulin and NPH insulin in one syringe. Which step is correct?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #287!

💉 Two insulins, one syringe. Which one goes in first?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Draw up regular insulin first

🧠 Rationale: Regular insulin is clear. NPH is cloudy.

Draw up clear before cloudy so NPH never gets into the regular vial.

Roll the NPH vial gently. Never shake it.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Mixing Insulin

💊 Insulin Types:

🔹 Regular: short acting, clear

🔹 NPH: intermediate acting, cloudy

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Inject air into NPH first, then regular

✅ Draw up regular, then NPH

✅ Roll NPH gently, do not shake

✅ Never mix glargine with other insulins

⚠️ Watch For:

🔹 Hypoglycemia at each insulin's peak

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Clear before cloudy!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: The nurse sees sawtooth waves between QRS complexes on the cardiac monitor. Which rhythm is this?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #288!

❤️ Sawtooth waves on the monitor. Can you name the rhythm?

This is a HIGH-YIELD cardiac question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Atrial flutter

🧠 Rationale: Atrial flutter shows regular sawtooth flutter waves.

Atrial fibrillation is irregularly irregular with no clear P waves.

V tach shows wide, fast QRS complexes.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Atrial Flutter

⚠️ Signs:

🔹 Palpitations

🔹 Shortness of breath

🔹 Fatigue or dizziness

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Check the client and vital signs first

✅ Expect rate control meds

✅ Anticoagulation to lower stroke risk

🚑 Escalate:

🔹 Unstable client may need cardioversion

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Flutter = sawtooth. Fib = fuzzy and irregular.

photos.question: Which lab value is the best indicator of kidney function?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #289!

🫘 One lab tells you the most about the kidneys. Which one?

This is a HIGH-YIELD renal question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Serum creatinine

🧠 Rationale: Creatinine comes from muscle at a steady rate.

Only the kidneys clear it, so it tracks kidney function best.

BUN can rise from dehydration, high protein or GI bleeding.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Kidney Labs

🧪 Normal Ranges (adult):

🔹 Creatinine: about 0.6 to 1.3 mg/dL

🔹 BUN: about 10 to 20 mg/dL

⚠️ Rising Creatinine Can Mean:

🔹 Acute kidney injury

🔹 Chronic kidney disease

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Track intake and output

✅ Check doses of kidney-cleared drugs

✅ Report a rising trend

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Creatinine = the kidney's report card!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: At what age does a healthy child usually begin walking alone?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #290!

👶 First steps! When do most kids start walking on their own?

This is a HIGH-YIELD pediatric growth and development question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — 12 to 15 months

🧠 Rationale: Most children walk alone around 12 to 15 months.

Cruising along furniture often starts around 9 to 10 months.

Not walking by 18 months needs follow-up.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Gross Motor Milestones

📅 Key Milestones:

🔹 Rolls over: 4 to 6 months

🔹 Sits without support: about 6 months

🔹 Pulls to stand: 9 to 10 months

🔹 Walks alone: 12 to 15 months

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Ask parents about milestones at each visit

✅ Report delays for screening

✅ Teach home safety as mobility grows

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Turn one, take a step, have some fun!

❤️ Follow @ryan__glass for daily NCLEX practice questions!

photos.question: A client with Parkinson disease starts carbidopa-levodopa. Which instruction should the nurse include?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #291!

🧠 This Parkinson med and your dinner plate do not mix well. Why?

This is a HIGH-YIELD neuro pharmacology question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: C — Avoid large high-protein meals near doses

🧠 Rationale: Protein competes with levodopa for absorption into the body and brain.

Large high-protein meals near doses can weaken the effect.

Never stop the drug suddenly.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Carbidopa-Levodopa

💊 Drug Class: Dopamine precursor combination

❤️ Primary Use: Parkinson disease

⚠️ Side Effects:

🔹 Orthostatic hypotension

🔹 Nausea

🔹 Involuntary movements

🔹 Dark urine or sweat, harmless

🚨 Patient Teaching:

✅ Rise slowly

✅ Do not stop suddenly

✅ Report new jerky movements

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Levodopa and steak? Keep them apart!

photos.question: Which vital sign change is expected during a normal pregnancy?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #292!

🤰 Pregnancy changes the vitals. Which change is normal?

This is a HIGH-YIELD maternity question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: A — Heart rate rises 10 to 15/min

🧠 Rationale: Blood volume rises about 40 to 50% in pregnancy.

The heart rate goes up about 10 to 15 beats per minute.

BP of 140/90 or higher is not normal and needs follow-up.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Normal Pregnancy Changes

❤️ Cardiac:

🔹 Heart rate up 10 to 15/min

🔹 BP often dips in the 2nd trimester

🩸 Blood:

🔹 Mild drop in hemoglobin from dilution

🚨 Report Right Away:

✅ BP 140/90 or higher

✅ Severe headache or vision changes

✅ Fever

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

More blood, faster beat!

photos.question: A client who is angry at a coworker tells the nurse, "My coworker hates me." Which defense mechanism is this?
photos.caption:
💊 NCLEX PRACTICE QUESTION #293!

🧩 Who is really angry here? Name that defense mechanism!

This is a HIGH-YIELD mental health question every nursing student should know! 🩺

👇 Comment your answer before checking!

.
.
.
.
.
.
.
.

✅ Correct Answer: B — Projection

🧠 Rationale: Projection means putting your own feelings onto someone else.

The client is angry but says the coworker hates them.

The feeling belongs to the client, not the coworker.

📚 NCLEX Must-Know: Defense Mechanisms

🧠 Know These:

🔹 Denial: refusing to accept reality

🔹 Projection: blaming your feelings on others

🔹 Regression: acting younger under stress

🔹 Sublimation: turning urges into healthy activity

🚨 Nursing Actions:

✅ Stay calm and nonjudgmental

✅ Help the client name their own feelings

💡 NCLEX MEMORY TIP:

Projection = a movie projector. Your feelings show up on someone else's screen!
